extracted.intended_audience: corporate finance teams, SEC reporting accountants, auditors, and securities lawyers preparing acquisition-related SEC filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing financial statements of acquired foreign businesses under SEC S-X Rule 3-05 and Form 20-F/Form 8-K requirements, including required periods, age limits, interim coverage, audit and reconciliation rules, and special FPI considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim financial statements: content and comparatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim financial statements should include comparative statements for the same period in the prior financial year (except comparative balance sheet information may be satisfied by presenting the year-end balance sheet). If not included in primary financial statements, a note must analyze changes in each caption of shareholders' equity. Interim statements should include selected note disclosures explaining events and changes significant to understanding changes in financial position and performance since the last annual reporting date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the company has published interim financial information covering a more current period than otherwise required by the standard, the more current interim information must be included. Companies are encouraged, but not required, to have interim statements reviewed by an independent auditor; if such a review is referred to, a copy of the auditor’s interim review report must be provided in the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3-05: number of annual periods required by significance
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-05(b) sets the number of financial periods required for Rule 3-05 financial statements; the period requirements are the same for domestic and foreign acquirees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
— Acquisition 20% or less significant: no periods required (no filing requirement).
— Acquisition >20% but ≤40% significant: one annual period required.
— Acquisition >40% significant: two annual periods required.
(Interim period rules are addressed separately.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Age requirements for domestic acquirees and non-foreign-business foreign entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The age requirements of Rule 3-05 financial statements for a domestic entity acquired by an FPI are the same as for a domestic registrant; the same age requirements apply to an acquisition of a foreign entity that does not meet the definition of a foreign business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These age requirements are set out in S-X Rule 3-01 and Rule 3-02 (see referenced guidance in section 4.2.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age requirements for acquired foreign businesses (Form 20-F governed)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the acquiree meets the definition of a foreign business, the age of the financial statements filed is determined under Item 8 of Form 20-F (not under S-X Rule 3-01 and Rule 3-02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 8.A of Form 20-F provides specific age requirements for financial statements of foreign businesses acquired by FPIs and domestic registrants when required under S-X Rule 3-05, and for filings on Forms S-4, F-4, and Rule 3-09 or 3-14/8-06 situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15-month requirement for annual financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3-05 financial statements include the acquiree’s audited financial statements for the most recently completed fiscal year, unless the Form 8-K is filed or the registration statement becomes effective within three months of that year-end; otherwise the prior fiscal year is required. This results in annual financial statements being no more than 15 months old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 15-month ‘ceiling’ ensures audited annual financial statements filed are not older than 15 months as of the filing/effective date. Examples in the guidance illustrate how filings within three months of year-end permit use of the prior fiscal year statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim financial statements: 9-month rule for foreign businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 3-05 requires interim financial statements that are as of a date within nine months of the filing of a Form 8-K or a registration statement’s effective date for foreign businesses (instead of the shorter domestic deadlines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the audited annual financial statements are within nine months, no interim statements are required; if not, interim statements that fall within the nine-month period are required and may be unaudited. The filing date (or due date) of the initial Form 8-K generally determines the age for Rule 3-05 statements filed on Form 8-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions extending age thresholds for specific offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: The 15-month period for audited financial statements is extended to 18 months, and the nine-month period for interim statements is extended to 12 months for registration statements for certain offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These offerings include exercise of outstanding rights granted pro rata to all existing security holders; dividend or interest reinvestment plans; and conversion of outstanding convertible securities or exercise of outstanding transferable warrants. (See Form 20-F Item 8 Instruction 2.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim coverage minimum: six-month requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If interim financial statements are required for an acquired foreign business, they must cover a period of at least six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An acquired foreign business in existence less than a year must include an audited balance sheet not more than nine months old and audited statements of income, stockholders’ equity, and cash flows for the period from inception to the balance sheet date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filings within three months after year-end: required periods
rubrics_metrics.description: If a filing (Form 8-K filing, registration statement effective date, or proxy mailing) is within three months after the foreign business’s year-end, the audited financial statements for the most recently completed fiscal year are not required; instead the prior fiscal year audited statements are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, unaudited interim financial statements must be within nine months of the filing/effective/mailing date; this can result in including interim statements for periods that ended before the most recently completed fiscal year. Examples illustrate application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filings beyond three months after year-end: required periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings made three months or more after an acquired foreign business’s year-end must include audited financial statements for the most recently completed fiscal year so annual statements do not exceed 15 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim statements are required if the filing/mailing/effective date is more than nine months after the acquired business’s fiscal year-end. Interim statements need not be audited and must cover at least six months. Generally no update needed if the omitted period is less than six months and the acquired business does not prepare interim statements under home-country requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of age for Form 8-K Rule 3-05 financials
rubrics_metrics.description: The age of Rule 3-05 financial statements filed on Form 8-K is generally determined as of the filing date (or due date) of the initial Form 8-K reporting the acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show that timely filing of the Form 8-K establishes the relevant date for comparing audited annual and interim statement ages and determining whether certain years or interim periods must be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: More current published financial information (Form 20-F Item 8.A.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, at the date of the document, the company has published interim financial information that covers a more current period than those otherwise required, the more current interim financial information must be included in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction 3 to Item 8.A.5 covers publications that contain at least revenue and income information, even if not a complete set of financial statements. If the only difference is greater currency (e.g., through Q2 vs Q1), the earlier period data need not be provided. Registrant must evaluate whether the more current information satisfies S-X Rule 3-05 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation and narrative differences for more current information
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant need not reconcile more current information provided under Item 8.A.5 of Form 20-F to US GAAP, but it must explain in narrative form differences in accounting principles and quantify material variations unless already quantified elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differences between foreign and US GAAP can be identified by cross reference to US GAAP reconciliation footnotes elsewhere in the filing; material new reconciling items must be quantified. If a new US accounting standard must be applied in the period of the updated information, disclose that fact; quantification not required if unreasonable cost or delay. FPIs using IFRS Accounting Standards-IASB are not required to provide the (a)/(b) information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of reconciling more current information to US GAAP
rubrics_metrics.description: If more current information included under Item 8.A.5 is also reconciled to US GAAP, the SEC staff believes interim financial statements have effectively been presented, which triggers additional update requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation of a US GAAP reconciliation with the more current information generally necessitates including comparative prior-year financial information and updating pro forma information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit standard requirement for Rule 3-05 foreign acquiree financials
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 8.A.2 of Form 20-F requires SEC filings to include financial statements audited under US GAAS. Therefore, Rule 3-05 financial statements of a foreign acquiree must be audited under US GAAS regardless of the basis (US GAAP, IFRS IASB, or home-country GAAP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If audited statements include reconciliations prepared under Items 17 or 18 of Form 20-F, those reconciliations also must be audited under US GAAS. The SEC staff will accept wording variations to comply with local report formats but encourages US GAAS report wording; the report must say the auditor performed the audit under US GAAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: FPI acquisition filing timing expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a domestic registrant or FPI acquires an FPI, the SEC staff expects the acquirer to file the Rule 3-05 financial statements no later than the date the acquired FPI is required to file its own Form 20-F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 20-F, when used as an annual report, is due within four months after an FPI’s fiscal year-end; if the acquirer must file a Form 8-K shortly after this four-month due date, Rule 3-05 statements may be required earlier than otherwise. Filing the acquired FPI’s Form 20-F early is permitted but not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: FPI proxy solicitation exemption and disclosure options
rubrics_metrics.description: An FPI must file a Form F-4 to register securities used in a business combination but is exempt from the proxy solicitation rules under Reg 14A (§240.3a12-3) and therefore need not file a Schedule 14A when a shareholder vote is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though proxy rules do not apply, information could be voluntarily disclosed on Form 6-K. Financial statement requirements of Form S-4 or F-4 apply to both the registrant and the target entity, with requirements depending on whether the target is a reporting company and who is voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation requirements for foreign targets in S-4/F-4
rubrics_metrics.description: If a foreign target’s financial statements are prepared on the basis of a comprehensive body of accounting principles other than US GAAP or IFRS IASB, a reconciliation to US GAAP under Item 17 of Form 20-F is required for all financial statements presented (unless reconciliation is unavailable or not obtainable without unreasonable cost or expense).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the target's financial statements have not previously been filed with the SEC, reconciliation is required only for the two most recent fiscal years and any interim periods required in the filing. See FRM 6410.2(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit requirements for nonreporting foreign targets previously audited under non-US GAAS
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonreporting foreign target’s financial statements for the years preceding the latest fiscal year were audited based on non-US GAAS, those periods’ financial statements must be audited based on US GAAS and filed on the registration statement if they were published for general distribution in the target’s home jurisdiction or elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff may consider granting relief on a case-by-case basis in unusual circumstances. Examples and further discussion appear in the referenced guidance (see FRM 4110.5).
